fr.elements: Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Terrain
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Open Terrain; Long Driveway
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with visible posts or reflectors on both sides to define the access point, especially in low-light or smoky conditions.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of parked vehicles and equipment to allow emergency vehicles to reach the detached structure without stopping.
• Maintain enough driveway width along its entire length for a fire apparatus or ambulance to pass through without obstruction.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area near the structures so emergency vehicles do not have to back out the full length of the driveway.
• Post the driveway distance and address on a sign visible from the road to help responders confirm the correct property on approach.
• Keep a gate, if present at the driveway entrance, unlocked or secured with a lock compatible with local fire department access tools.
• Identify a staging area on the open terrain that is accessible from the driveway and large enough for multiple emergency vehicles to operate simultaneously.
• Mark any soft ground, drainage ditches, or low spots along the driveway edge that could cause a heavy vehicle to get stuck.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Ground Vegetation; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the house on all sides.
• Remove shrubs growing immediately around any outbuildings or detached structures.
• Keep ground vegetation mowed or cut short in the open areas surrounding the house.
• Thin scattered shrubs between the house and the property boundaries to create open gaps between plants.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and shrubs on both sides.
• Remove any dead or dry ground vegetation that has accumulated along the driveway.
• Maintain open ground between shrub groupings so plants are not touching or connecting to each other.
• Keep shrubs separated from any fences, woodpiles, or stored materials near the house.
